Problem

DSATokenToKVPool.move_kv_cache (srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py) moves the DSA indexer cache with:

for index_k in self.index_k_with_scale_buffer:   # PAGE-indexed: (num_pages, page_size*(...))
    index_k[tgt_loc_flat] = index_k[src_loc_flat]  # tgt/src are per-TOKEN locations

index_k_with_scale_buffer is page-indexed (dim-0 is num_pages, with page_size tokens packed along
dim-1), but tgt_loc/src_loc are token locations. This is correct only for page_size == 1; for
page_size == 64 (all CUDA DSA) it indexes the page dimension with token indices → wrong rows / OOB → silent
indexer-cache corruption. It is reached only via move_accept_tokens_to_target_kvcache on the topk>1
tree-draft path (srt/speculative/spec_utils.py); the topk==1 chain (e.g. GLM-5.2) never hits it, so it is
latent today.

Fix

Add a fail-fast guard at the top of the method: for page_size != 1, raise NotImplementedError (before any
move, preserving the method's all-or-nothing contract) explaining that a page-aware move is required before
tree-drafting (topk>1) is enabled on DSA. The page_size == 1 path and the base MLA super().move_kv_cache
(token-indexed, correct) are unchanged. A page-aware rewrite is deliberately out of scope — this stops silent
corruption cheaply until tree-drafting on DSA is actually wired up.

Testing (all pass)

test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_dsa_move_kv_cache_guard.py — GPU-free, 2/2 PASSED:

method asserts
test_move_kv_cache_raises_for_page_size_gt_1 page_size ∈ {16, 64} raises NotImplementedError (fails on pre-fix code, which silently mis-moves); the 16 case pins != 1 vs a wrong == 64
test_move_kv_cache_page_size_1_moves_without_guard page_size == 1 does not raise and moves the correct row

fix(dsa): guard move_kv_cache against page-indexed corruption for pag…
569286b 
…e_size>1

DSATokenToKVPool.move_kv_cache moved the DSA indexer cache with:

    for index_k in self.index_k_with_scale_buffer:
        index_k[tgt_loc_flat] = index_k[src_loc_flat]

but index_k_with_scale_buffer is PAGE-indexed -- _index_buffer_shape is
(num_pages, page_size * (index_head_dim + ...)), so dim-0 is pages, with
page_size tokens packed along dim-1 -- while tgt_loc/src_loc are per-TOKEN
locations. The per-token row copy is only correct when page_size == 1. For
page_size > 1 it indexes the wrong rows and, since token locations exceed
num_pages (~size/page_size), reads/writes out of bounds. The base class'
maybe_detect_oob checks the token size_limit, not the page count, so it does
not catch this. This is wrong on all CUDA DSA (page_size is always 64) and on
HIP preshuffle (page_size % 16 == 0); only HIP-legacy (page_size == 1) is safe.

The bug is latent today: this method is reached only via the topk>1 speculative
tree-draft path (move_accept_tokens_to_target_kvcache). GLM runs topk == 1
(chain), so it never hits it, which is why no corruption has been observed.

This adds an explicit guard (raise NotImplementedError for page_size != 1)
rather than a full page-aware move. Correctly moving the page-packed index-K
buffer per token is non-trivial (each token is a dim-1 sub-slice of a page,
fp8 key + fp32 scale), and the path is currently dead. A guard is the cheapest
correct stopgap: it makes the wrong path fail loudly instead of silently
corrupting KV memory, and documents that a page-aware move must land before
tree-drafting (topk>1) is enabled on DSA. The page_size == 1 path and the base
super().move_kv_cache() MLA move (token-indexed, correct) are unchanged.

Adds test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_dsa_move_kv_cache_guard.py: a GPU-free
unit test asserting page_size > 1 raises and page_size == 1 still moves.
